executive_summary: lib/eva/archplan-upsert.js's upsertArchPlan() unconditionally hardcodes status='active' and chairman_approved=true on every write (lines 121-122), with no parameter to override it -- so any architecture plan written by any caller is instantly claimed chairman-approved. LEAD-phase Explore + VALIDATION sub-agent review confirmed this is real and found a directly analogous PRIOR FIX already shipped on the VISION side (QF-20260702-262): vision-upsert.js exposes an approved boolean (default true for backward compat) and vision-command.mjs makes the choice MANDATORY at the CLI (hard-errors without --approved|--draft) -- but architecture plans never received either leg. 200 of 235 live rows come from the CLI (archplan-command.mjs), which has zero approval flags today, so a helper-level fix alone would leave the dominant write path unaffected. This SD adds both legs to architecture plans, closes a compounding defect where stage-17-doc-generation.js writes an ACTIVE chairman-approved plan against a DRAFT unapproved parent vision (live today on ARCH-ALTIFYAI-001, the chairman-watched AltifyAI test-cargo venture), stamps the previously-unwritten chairman_approved_at column, and designs a separate gated promotion (draft->active) updater using only existing columns -- including a self-approval guard (promoter != created_by) that meaningfully advances ratification a588adba's reviewer-not-author requirement even before the approved_by column (which does not exist on either table and is named, not built, in this SD per its own chairman-ceremony scope rule) is added in a future migration.

functional_requirements.title: Add an approved parameter to upsertArchPlan(), mirroring vision-upsert.js
functional_requirements.description: Add an optional `approved` parameter to lib/eva/archplan-upsert.js's upsertArchPlan() signature, default `true` (preserving backward compatibility for existing callers that don't pass it -- matching vision-upsert.js's own default-true precedent). When `approved !== false`, write status='active', chairman_approved=true, chairman_approved_at=now() (see FR-4). When `approved === false`, write status='draft', chairman_approved=false, chairman_approved_at=null.
acceptance_criteria: upsertArchPlan({..., approved: false}) writes status='draft', chairman_approved=false, chairman_approved_at=null

upsertArchPlan({...}) with approved omitted writes status='active', chairman_approved=true, chairman_approved_at set (byte-identical outward behavior to today for existing callers, except the new timestamp -- see FR-4)
upsertArchPlan({..., approved: true}) is explicitly equivalent to omitting the parameter
No existing caller's positional/keyword usage requires a code change

functional_requirements.title: Make the approval choice mandatory at the CLI, mirroring vision-command.mjs
functional_requirements.description: scripts/eva/archplan-command.mjs's upsert subcommand currently calls upsertArchPlan with no approval-related argument (its own help text falsely claims 'after chairman approval' -- nothing enforces this). Mirror vision-command.mjs's mandatory --approved|--draft flag pattern exactly: hard-error with a clear message if neither flag is passed (no default-approve fallback at the CLI layer, even though the underlying helper defaults true for other programmatic callers), and reuse vision-upsert.js's exported rejectStringFlagValue guard so a string 'false' can't coerce to a truthy approved value.
acceptance_criteria: Running the upsert subcommand with neither --approved nor --draft hard-errors before any DB write, with a message naming both flags (mirroring vision-command.mjs:140's wording)
--draft writes a draft, unapproved plan
--approved writes an active, chairman_approved plan with chairman_approved_at stamped
Passing an invalid/string coercion (e.g. --approved false) is rejected via rejectStringFlagValue, not silently coerced to true
Update the upsert subcommand's help text to accurately describe the required flag, removing the false 'after chairman approval' claim

functional_requirements.title: Fix stage-17-doc-generation.js's two unfixed architecture-plan call sites
functional_requirements.description: lib/eva/stage-templates/analysis-steps/stage-17-doc-generation.js already fixed its VISION call site (line 284, approved:false, under a QF-20260702-262 comment) but its two upsertArchPlan call sites (lines ~373, ~395) still pass nothing approval-related, so this file currently writes a DRAFT unapproved vision immediately followed by an ACTIVE chairman-approved architecture plan claiming alignment to it -- an internally incoherent state independent of any downstream security implication, live today on real venture plans including ARCH-ALTIFYAI-001. Pass approved:false at both call sites, mirroring the vision call site exactly.
acceptance_criteria: Both upsertArchPlan call sites in stage-17-doc-generation.js pass approved:false

A new regression-guard test (mirroring stage-17-doc-generation.test.js's existing QF-262 vision guard at line ~174) asserts both arch-plan writes produce status='draft', chairman_approved=false -- and fails if that assertion is reverted (mutation-tested)
Existing stage-17-doc-generation.test.js suite passes unmodified in all other assertions

functional_requirements.title: Stamp chairman_approved_at whenever chairman_approved flips true
functional_requirements.description: chairman_approved_at exists on eva_architecture_plans (nullable timestamptz) but is never written by upsertArchPlan today -- only 4 of 211 currently-approved rows carry a timestamp. Set it to now() whenever the write results in chairman_approved=true (both the approved-by-default path and an explicit approved:true), null when chairman_approved=false. No DDL required -- the column already exists.
acceptance_criteria: Every write with the resulting chairman_approved=true also sets chairman_approved_at to the write's own timestamp
Every write with chairman_approved=false sets chairman_approved_at=null
A unit test proves this for both branches

functional_requirements.title: Design a separate, gated promotion (draft->active) updater for architecture plans, with a self-approval guard
functional_requirements.description: There is currently no code path anywhere that promotes an eva_architecture_plans row from draft to active/chairman_approved via UPDATE (only 3 INSERT/upsert writes exist total). Writing plans as draft-only with no promotion path would itself be a regression (artifact-persistence-service.js's ADR-attachment and the planning-completeness PLAN-TO-EXEC gate would silently degrade forever for any plan legitimately reviewed and approved after the fact). Design and implement a new, separate function (NOT inside upsertArchPlan) that UPDATEs an existing draft row to status='active', chairman_approved=true, chairman_approved_at=now(), modeled on lib/eva/stage-execution-worker.js's _autoApproveCloneVision UPDATE pattern (lines ~3935/4017) but adding a genuine self-approval guard per ratification a588adba's reviewer-not-author requirement: the function must accept a `promotedBy` identity and REFUSE the promotion when promotedBy equals the plan row's own created_by (using the EXISTING created_by column -- this meaningfully advances the reviewer!=author requirement even before an approved_by column exists to persist WHO approved; see FR-6). The function must also satisfy eva_architecture_plans' existing UPDATE-only quality-advancement trigger (trg_enforce_archplan_quality_advancement, which requires quality_checked=true) -- do not attempt to bypass or weaken this trigger; a promotion attempt on a row with quality_checked=false must fail with the trigger's own error, not a swallowed/silent no-op.
acceptance_criteria: A new promotion function exists, callable independently of upsertArchPlan, that UPDATEs status/chairman_approved/chairman_approved_at on an existing row
The function refuses (with a clear, non-silent error) when promotedBy === the target row's created_by
The function succeeds when promotedBy differs from created_by and the row's quality_checked=true
The function's UPDATE against a row with quality_checked=false fails via the existing DB trigger (not a separately-implemented, potentially-divergent application-level check)
Unit tests cover: successful promotion, self-approval refusal, and the quality-trigger failure path

functional_requirements.title: Name the approved_by migration need; do not implement it (chairman ceremony)
functional_requirements.description: Neither eva_architecture_plans nor eva_vision_documents has an approved_by column, and no DDL is authorized in this SD per its own scope text ('New columns or tables are a chairman ceremony: PLAN names the files and stops there'). Document the specific, minimal migration needed (a nullable text/uuid approved_by column on eva_architecture_plans, written by FR-5's promotion function alongside the existing chairman_approved_at) as a named, deferred follow-up -- do not write or apply any migration file in this SD.
acceptance_criteria: The PR description (or a docs note) names the exact column, table, and write-site (FR-5's promotion function) that a future chairman-ceremony-gated migration SD should add
No migration file, DDL statement, or schema change of any kind is included in this SD's diff

technical_requirements.title: No unconditional default flip
technical_requirements.description: upsertArchPlan's approved parameter must default to true (backward-compatible), not false -- an unconditional flip would silently degrade artifact-persistence-service.js's ADR-attachment consumer and the planning-completeness gate for every future SD unless FR-5's promotion path is used deliberately. The CLI's mandatory-choice requirement (FR-2) is what actually closes the governance gap for the dominant write path, not the helper default.

technical_requirements.title: No DDL
technical_requirements.description: This SD ships entirely against existing columns (status, chairman_approved, chairman_approved_at, created_by all already exist on eva_architecture_plans). FR-6 documents the one deferred migration need; it is not implemented here.

technical_requirements.title: trust-elevation.js safety already verified, no change needed there
technical_requirements.description: LEAD-phase VALIDATION independently measured that lib/eva/bridge/trust-elevation.js's chairman_approved AND-guard cannot be broken by this fix into a stuck-venture state: every real venture's trust elevation is carried by its vision's chairman_approved status regardless of the arch-plan limb, historical elevations are 100% vision-attributed, and the check is mint-time-only/idempotent. No code change to trust-elevation.js is required or in scope.

test_scenarios.expected: Row written with status='draft', chairman_approved=false, chairman_approved_at=null
Row written with status='active', chairman_approved=true, chairman_approved_at set to the write time
Hard error before any DB write; no row created/updated
Rejected via rejectStringFlagValue, not silently treated as true
Both produce status='draft', chairman_approved=false; mutation-tested regression guard fails if approved:false is reverted at either call site

test_scenarios.scenario: Promotion function called with promotedBy === row.created_by
test_scenarios.expected: Refused with a clear error; row unchanged

test_scenarios.scenario: Promotion function called with promotedBy != row.created_by, quality_checked=true
test_scenarios.expected: Row promoted: status='active', chairman_approved=true, chairman_approved_at set

test_scenarios.scenario: Promotion function called against a row with quality_checked=false
test_scenarios.expected: UPDATE fails via the existing trg_enforce_archplan_quality_advancement trigger, not a separate application check

test_scenarios.scenario: Full pre-existing archplan-upsert.test.js and stage-17-doc-generation.test.js suites

acceptance_criteria: No architecture plan can be written chairman-approved via the CLI (the dominant, 200/235-row write path) without an explicit --approved choice
stage-17-doc-generation.js no longer writes an approved architecture plan against an unapproved parent vision
A promotion path exists for legitimately reviewing and approving a draft plan, with a genuine self-approval guard using the existing created_by column
chairman_approved_at is populated going forward for every newly-approved plan
No DDL is introduced; the approved_by migration need is named for a future chairman-ceremony SD
trust-elevation.js's venture trust-tier elevation guard is unaffected in behavior for any currently-trusted venture

risks.risk: RESOLVED DURING LEAD (recorded for history): an initial concern that tightening chairman_approved to be genuinely meaningful could cause trust-elevation.js to block ventures that previously passed via the rubber-stamped arch-plan limb.
risks.mitigation: VALIDATION measured directly: every real venture's elevation is carried by the vision limb regardless; historical elevations are 100% vision-attributed; the check is mint-time-only and idempotent so no already-trusted venture is affected. No code change to trust-elevation.js needed.

risks.risk: A helper-level-only fix (approved param with no CLI enforcement) would leave the dominant 200/235-row CLI write path unaffected, failing to actually close the gap the SD's title describes.
risks.mitigation: FR-2 makes the choice mandatory at the CLI layer specifically, mirroring vision-command.mjs's already-proven pattern rather than relying on a default alone.

risks.risk: A promotion function without any self-approval guard would satisfy the mechanical draft/active toggle but not ratification a588adba's substantive reviewer-not-author requirement.
risks.mitigation: FR-5 requires the promotion function to compare promotedBy against the row's existing created_by column and refuse on match -- a real, enforced guard achievable without the deferred approved_by column.

risks.risk: eva_architecture_plans' UPDATE-only quality-advancement trigger (missing an INSERT-leg equivalent, unlike eva_vision_documents) means 38 live rows are already chairman_approved=true with quality_checked=false -- a pre-existing gap this SD does not close.
risks.mitigation: Out of scope, flagged for a separate ticket per LEAD-phase VALIDATION's recommendation. This SD's promotion function correctly relies on and respects the existing trigger rather than working around it.

consumers: lib/eva/bridge/trust-elevation.js (reads chairman_approved for venture trust-tier elevation -- behavior verified unaffected for real ventures)
scripts/modules/handoff/executors/plan-to-exec/gates/planning-completeness.js (reads status='active' as a non-blocking warning input)
scripts/eva/archplan-command.mjs (CLI, gains the mandatory approval choice)
dependencies: trg_enforce_archplan_quality_advancement (existing UPDATE trigger, relied on not modified)
data_contracts: none -- no schema change; FR-6 names a future migration need only
observability_rollout: Verified via the unit/regression test suites named in FR-1 through FR-5; no new dashboard or monitoring surface is in scope

system_architecture.summary: Two additive legs mirroring the already-proven vision-upsert/vision-command pattern (helper-level default-true param + CLI-level mandatory choice), a call-site fix closing a live incoherent-state defect, a cheap timestamp fix, and a new, separate, gated promotion updater with a genuine self-approval guard built from existing columns -- no schema change.
